native_result.query: How were the phases of the Middle Neolithic (3400-3000 BCE) and Younger Neolithic (2900-2300 BCE) characterized in terms of the first principal component in a PCA on the forms of capital analyzed in hundred-year time slices?
native_result.HypoA: During the Middle Neolithic (3400-3000 BCE) and Younger Neolithic (2900-2300 BCE), both phases are primarily associated with negative values on the first principal component (PC1). This Principal component analysis (PCA) is on the forms of capital. The values of the individual elements of the forms of capital form the attributes.
native_result.HypoB: Both the Middle Neolithic (3400-3000 BCE) and the Younger Neolithic (2900-2300 BCE) occupy the low-capital-intensity end of PC1 (sign fixed positive toward overall capital intensity, corr = +0.557; PC1 explains 30.3% of variance). The Middle Neolithic shows a declining PC1 trajectory (mean -1.37; -0.58 at 3400 BCE falling to -1.78 at 3000 BCE, about -0.26 units per century), whereas the Younger Neolithic shows a fluctuating but recovering trajectory (mean -1.12, 0.26 units higher; -1.50 at 2900 BCE rising to -0.41 at 2300 BCE, about +0.12 units per century, with local recoveries at 2700 and 2300 BCE). PC1 increases are driven by copper/gold (+0.41 loading), pottery decoration (+0.38) and depots (+0.34), while the negative scores of both phases are depressed mainly by pottery form (-0.35), axes/celts (-0.24), amber (-0.24) and sickles (-0.15); both phases remain far below later Bronze Age PC1 levels (+1.9 to +4.4). Bin-level PC1 correlates strongly with pollen-based landscape openness (r = 0.71), but within the Middle Neolithic openness rises (+1.93) while PC1 falls, indicating a within-phase decoupling of capital intensity from environmental openness.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Loaded capital.csv (comma decimals): 39 rows x 15 cols, 100-year bins BCE 4300-500 (positive counting backward; verified identical to time_series_data.csv *_inter at CE=-BCE), 12 Z columns, no missing values, group labels MN=3400-3000 and SG=2900-2300 matching the question's phases. 2) Correlation-matrix PCA on the 12 re-standardized Z columns over the full 4300-500 BCE series via numpy SVD (sklearn unavailable). 3) PC1 sign convention: positive correlation with the mean of the 12 Z (corr = +0.557, no flip needed). 4) Extracted PC1 per 100-year bin (analysis/pc1_by_bin.csv) and loadings (analysis/pc1_loadings.csv). 5) Characterized MN (3400,3300,3200,3100,3000) and SG (2900..2300): means (-1.374 vs -1.117), ranges (1.199 vs 1.187), per-century trends (-0.259 vs +0.120), drivers via loadings. 6) Secondary context: pollen openness (Belau/Woserin MEAN, decimal=','), bin-level corr(PC1, MEAN) = 0.711 (n=36 bins), within-phase MN decoupling documented. Script: analysis/pca_capital_phases.py.
